findings.note: PlanShards keeps an (ShardPlan, error) signature but every return path is a nil error, so the error handling at internal/taskdone/review.go:109 and internal/prready/review.go:111 is dead code. The over-limit case (shards.go:193) returns an empty plan with nil error, indistinguishable at the call site from 'not sharded'; it is only explained because contextprofile.riskReasons separately raises ReasonDiffOversize (internal/contextprofile/profile.go:143).

evidence.note: signature returns error that is never non-nil

findings.note: Mislabelled structured field: the id-conflict error passes the run id as the value of the "line" key, while every other ERR_RUNS_JSONL error uses "line" for a line number (record.go:166). A consumer keying on Fields["line"] gets a run id here, which is a type confusion in the CLI error envelope.

evidence.note: same key used for an actual line number

findings.note: Torn-tail repair can discard a concurrent row. The comment at record.go:180-187 states the second writer (state.AppendJSONL) takes no lock; readRows snapshots the file with os.ReadFile, and f.Truncate(t.offset) then cuts the file back to that snapshot's offset, so a complete row appended by the unlocked writer between the read and the truncate is lost. The O_APPEND write itself is safe; only the truncate path carries the race, and only when a torn fragment exists.

evidence.note: f.Truncate(t.offset) based on a pre-read snapshot offset
advisory flock excludes only writers that also take it

findings.note: The newly added docs/metareview/fsm exclusion has no test. TestCollectExcludesShardResults only creates and asserts a docs/metareview/shards result; nothing asserts an FSM export bundle stays out of the learning diff, so a later regression in that pattern pair would not be caught.

evidence.note: test covers only the shards exclusion

findings.note: PlanSourceHash is exported and its first parameter is discarded (_ Profile); the only caller in the repository is internal/contextprofile/plan_test.go:87. It is an exported surface that exists solely to assert that the profile does not affect the hash, which the delegation to SourceDiffHash already makes structurally true.

evidence.note: exported wrapper with an ignored Profile parameter

findings.note: record.go's unconditional import of syscall (syscall.Flock, LOCK_EX/LOCK_UN) makes the package unix-only. Checked against the rest of the tree: internal/fsm/cmdexec and internal/fsm/machine/sidecar already depend on syscall.SysProcAttr.Setpgid and syscall.O_NOFOLLOW, so this is the established platform assumption of the FSM packages, not a regression introduced here.

evidence.note: var flock = syscall.Flock, matching existing unix-only FSM packages
